name: roach
about: Chain ragdoll body for ARMAGEDOM's original-roach (the sewer and ash roaches and the nest guard are recipes on it). Same 27-bone roach rig as the spider, so the same 14 capsules: body (root, kinematic), thorax, head, abdomen, and 6 legs: the front and rear pairs have two capsules (upper = leg to shin, lower = shin to foot), the middle pair one (leg to foot). Bones without a part (root, antennae, mandibles) follow their parent bone in the scene graph; the shin and foot of a middle leg ride the leg. Part ids equal the spider's, so the roach shares the spider's hit-reaction family. Every number is here; src/chain.mjs holds none.
placeholder_note: radii, masses, joint limits and the two synthetic end points (abdomen_tip, head_tip) are PLACEHOLDERS to tune on Dom's phone and the clips; only the bone positions are measured. Radii are smaller than the spider's (a roach is flat and wide, a spider round) and the abdomen is shorter. Every joint is a ball joint with a wide cone, so a leg can curl under the body: the hinge row (hinge_flex_z) only tests the z direction of a bend and cannot say 'curl up' for a leg that points sideways.
scale_source: Armagedom Web/src/data/creatureDefinitions.json original-roach scale.model = 3 (character 1.265 and visual 1.3225 are applied by the actor wrapper on top and are NOT in this scale, the same choice as the spider and salamander). Bones and radii below are in model units, the row is in metres at this scale.
mass_assumption: placeholder: a body about 1.3 m long and 1.2 m across the legs at x3 (abdomen tip to head tip 0.46 model units, foot to foot 0.41); a flat chitin body is light for its size, 31 kg total is an estimate (abdomen 9, body 6, thorax 5, head 2, legs 9.2), lighter than the spider's 47 kg. Tune against how heavy the fall should feel.
